ety.text: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit द्वार (dvāra). Doublet of बार (bār) and दर (dar).
Inherited from Prakrit णप्पइ (ṇappaï). Related to ज्ञान (jñān), ज्ञापन (jñāpan), and ज्ञापक (jñāpak). Cognate to Punjabi ਨਾਪਣਾ (nāpṇā), Odia ନାପିବା (nāpibā).
Borrowed from Classical Persian ناراض (nā-rāz), from ناـ (nā-) + Arabic رَاضٍ (rāḍin). By surface analysis, ना- (nā-) + राज़ी (rāzī). Compare Bengali নারাজ (naraj) and Marathi नाराज (nārāj).

s.g: the seventh (last) note of the Indian solfege, denoted नि (ni)
